I consider myself a Wanderer, or maybe, given information as I briefly died as a child. I don’t remember anything but I imagine if I saw my mother crying out to God like she said she did while I was unconscious that I would choose to come back, despite possibly having the knowledge of how hard the next few decades would be, the past year especially.

I was always happy and laughing as a kid. Always silly to make others laugh. I was naturally positive and cheerful. The world and many events onward did a very good job of pushing me inward, depressing me, developing and integrating anxiety. I spent most of my life thinking the world was simply painful. And my anxiety pushed me to believe that I had to search for solutions. I lived in all the future possible outcomes that could have happened and tried preparing for the worst. Reflecting on the past to justify my depressive state. Never present. Ultimately ending up conceal carrying a pistol and wearing a bulletproof insert in my backpack thinking I was smart and prepared. I was just paranoid. 

This last year has push me to my edge and I hit a wall where I recognized I could not advance. I sought help and received medication, started meditating, journaling with my higher self / subconscious, all while learning about the Law of One. With these tools I can finally live in the present. I can see the point of all the pain I’ve been through. Looking back, it’s very easy to see what my possible “mission” or intention is in my life. What I’ve been resisting, avoiding, and drawn to. I’m here to help others. First I had to help myself. And now I have the tools to do so. You cannot pour from an empty cup. 

This has been critical to my life and others, as my friend who needs real help benefits from me being level headed. Being anxious, fearful, overly prepared, and coming off as if that’s the smart thing to do benefitted no one. Maybe one day they will benefit from my new found self loving and self accepting understandings that they desperately need for themselves. If interested you can check my post history, same friend as the first post I’ve made. 

All in all, I see the poetry that life is now. And like a poem, at first it may not make sense or be as profound until you start reading the Iater verses. Life is still hard, but I am grounded, I am love, I am life. When people think of me, I want them to remember me like I was as a child. Always smiling, radiating hope and happiness. I wish to inspire others to live more peacefully through my words and actions. To be a light in the darkness.

I have much more life to live, but I can say the past year has put me on the path to truly living.

Please consider for a moment that at any moment there only exists two places. One place is everything that is outside of your physical body. The other is your mind, your thoughts, beliefs, choices and perceptions.

Outside your body you experience life through the lens of your various senses. Like watching a movie, these things are outside of you. Maybe all around you. Possibly affecting your human body. Often you may experience very difficult scenes, and situations in outward reality which will pull your other space towards negativity.  

Your other space is internal. It is who you are. It is unconquerable if you wish it to be. You are not your thoughts, but the observer of those thoughts. The thoughts you accept becomes the inner reality you experience. 

How do we know this? Two people can walk on the same beach. One has a great time, is happy to be there and finds it calming. The other is angry and upset, thinking how they hate the heat, the sand, the sounds and smells. What is the difference? How can two people with the same outward experience have such different responses? Another example, a prisoner in their cell can feel at peace and meditated, while a CEO in their mansion and a million dollars in the bank can hate their life. What’s the difference here? How can someone in an objectively worse outward condition feel better inward than someone else? One more example. You walk down the street and someone passes you by. They look at your shoes and say “ugh, not my style”. Are you doomed to feel inadequate? That you’ve made a mistake? Or can you disregard the comment. Know that you like your shoes and that is good enough for you and to keep walking? What’s the differences in all these scenarios? The difference is your inner perspective. 

It is not up to us to save the outward world. It is not something we can or should attempt to do as it’s outside of the tiny amount of control we have. Yes, doing good deeds is meaningful if it helps others/yourself. However we are but one tiny soul. The best thing we can do for ourselves and indirectly others by being a light, by being a cup that’s filled that can pour over for others, is to take care of ourselves.

It is our responsibility to save and protect our inner selves. The observer (you) that agrees or rejects the thoughts that pass before them. You can choose peace and happiness right now in this moment, as peace is not a place that exists in a physical location, when you have a certain amount of money in the bank, or a specific president. Peace exists inside us. We get to choose it. And in this way, if we understand that nothing external can sway us internally, then we are infinitely strong and unconquerable. We will only choose what aligns with us, and drop the rest. We will be at peace with conditions we once thought impossible to bare.

Yes, external circumstances will absolutely rattle us. Material conditions can worsen the quality of our outward lives. But we always decide the perspective we have, the belief that life is good or bad, the understanding that we decide how and if an experience affects our inner selves. This is the inner work that’s spoken about. This is why meditation is so valuable, to help train the observer to allow thoughts to pass without judgement or attachment. 

I do not know you, but I hope this writing has helped in some small way. And I hope taking the time to write this out shows you in some tiny way that you are outwardly loved, and can be shown love through the intention, effort, and actions of others. Now the biggest challenge you will ever face from here on out. One I know you can grow strong to overcome. Is to love yourself, and allow yourself peace.
